newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso recovers on rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso recovers on rate hike.

text.p: *Central Bank raises borrowing rate to 11.5 from 11 pct
The Philippine peso recovered on Monday after the Central Bank raised its key overnight borrowing rate for the second time in less than a week, dealers said.
It ended at 26.365 from the previous close of 26.374. The day's average was 26.367 from 26.374, with volume lower at $210.8 million from $315.8 million.
As a result of the rate hike, heavy inflows of arbitrage money went through foreign banks, dealers said.

Moreover, local banks were returning the dollars they bought from the Central Bank after the rate increase early on Monday. Last Wednesday, the Central Bank lifted its overnight borrowing rate by 0.75 percentage points to 11 percent.
Banks had become jittery over capital flight after last week's sharp drop on share prices.
Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza told Reuters: "This (the raising of the Central Bank's key overnight rate) is a temporary action. We will continue to monitor the market daily."
In late trade, the Central Bank had to step in and bought about $102 million at 26.364/26.368, traders said.
Traders said the Central Bank is likley to maintain its key rate at 11.5 percent on Tuesday until the local equities market shows a stable trend towards recovery.
"The peso will continue to strengthen on Tuesday," a dealer said, adding it could trade in the range of 26.36/26.365.
